messages:
Maria (Product): quick sync — we need final shape for the Q2 contract terms we'll present to Beta customers tomorrow. main open items: commit window length, onboarding credits, overage forgiveness, and the priority-routing add-on pricing.
AJ (Finance): high level: prefer 3 commit windows (monthly, quarterly, annual). pricing tiers should map to commit depth. monthly = baseline, quarterly = 7% discount, annual = 20% discount. onboarding credits should be timeboxed and applied as dollar credits not tokens.
Devin (Sales): customers are asking for per-route soft caps (so they can protect production routes) and a temporary grace for overages for first 30 days post-launch. ideally a simple rule: first 30 days we bill at estimated usage or at-list, then adjust.
Sarah (Legal): we need explicit language around overage forgiveness: "first 30 days post-onboarding, provider will not levy penalty fees for usage > committed volume; customer will be billed at list rate and may receive adjustment via credit if validated." That avoids open-ended indemnities.
Tom (Eng): operational constraints: priority-routing add-on (fast lane) requires dedicated routing pools and affects autoscaling. We need to reserve capacity so SLOs aren't violated for baseline customers. That means we should price the add-on to cover a minimum reserved slot cost (~$X per reserved GPU-hour).
AJ (Finance): can we express add-on pricing as "per-concurrent-slot" + flat monthly minimum? e.g., $250/slot/month + usage? keeps it simple and ties to cost.
Maria (Product): draft proposal from product POV: 3 tiers — Foundation, Scale, Performance. Foundation: self-serve, metered, no reserved slots. Scale: includes light reserved capacity (1 slot), 10% lower usage rates, limited priority lanes. Performance: 5 slots, SLA, faster support, deeper discount. Priority-routing add-on available for Foundation/Scale as purchasable slots.
Devin (Sales): call out that mid-market wants a mid-tier that has can-be-reserved but also burst credits. We should include a small burst-credit pool (e.g., 100M tokens/month) for Scale that can be purchased for Performance at larger sizes.
Sarah (Legal): we also need clear termination and roll-back language for reserved slots: if customer reduces commit we should allow a cooldown period (30 days) where reserved capacity is still charged unless swapped. Also require 30-day notice for downsize on annual contracts.
Tom (Eng): rollout concerns: priority-routing requires rollout gating by region. we can support US-EAST immediately, EU in Q3. must be explicit in docs and sales materials to avoid promises outside regions.
OpsBot: deploy-bot: new billing-pricing-config.yml applied to staging at 2026-03-21T09:12:02Z (CI #3421) :white_check_mark:
Maria (Product): launch criteria checklist proposal (short):
- pricing matrix published in docs and sales portal
- billing integration validated in sandbox (refunds/credits tested)
- SLA wording reviewed by legal
- pilot customer onboarded and uses priority-routing in US-EAST
- telemetry: token-level cost breakdown and slot utilization live
- rollout note for regions (EU delayed)
AJ (Finance): gating metrics to allow public launch: 3 pilot customers on annual or quarterly commits covering >= $75k ARR, billing tests pass, and projected 2% margin impact from reserved slot amortization.
Devin (Sales): I'll confirm two pilot commitments by EOD with ACME and Nimbly, pushing for quarterly to start.
Sarah (Legal): I'll push the overage forgiveness clause and the downsize notice into the Term Sheet template and upload by 5pm.
Tom (Eng): I'll add region gating flags and a perf test for priority routing into the release checklist. ETA EOD.
Maria (Product): decision for tomorrow's deck: keep three tiers + priority-routing as an add-on priced per-slot with monthly minimum. include onboarding credit as one-time dollar credit applied within first billing cycle, and explicit 30-day grace policy for overages with manual review. any objections?
AJ (Finance): no objections. please include an example price calculation in the deck.
Devin (Sales): 👍 one ask: include a sample SLA credit table (latency tiers -> % credit) so customers can see tradeoffs.
Sarah (Legal): +1 on SLA credit table, will provide standard template.
Maria (Product): great — I'll update the deck and ping for final review at 16:30. thanks all.
